nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Lagerstroemia: After Magnus von Lagerstrom (1696-1759) Swedish merchant, director of the Swedish East India Company, who supplied Carl Linnaeus with plants he collected
- parviflora: From the Latin parvus - 'small' and flora - 'flowers'

stem_bark.text: The bark of Lagerstroemia parviflora is brown-grey in colour. It is exfoliating in long, narrow vertical flakes pealing off, leaving a light yellow colour underneath the exposed bark. The bark becomes even more intensely flaky as it gets older.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Lagerstroemia parviflora is brown-grey in colour. 
It is exfoliating in long, narrow vertical flakes pealing off, leaving a light yellow colour underneath the exposed bark. 
The bark becomes even more intensely flaky as it gets older.

seed.text: The seeds of Lagerstroemia parviflora are many in each capsule. The seeds have a terminal wing with a thick curved back. They are about 1.5 cm long and 0.5 cm wide.
seed.text_html:
The seeds of Lagerstroemia parviflora are many in each capsule. 
The seeds have a terminal wing with a thick curved back. 
They are about 1.5 cm long and 0.5 cm wide.

fruit.text: The fruits of Lagerstroemia parviflora are leathery 3 or 4-valved capsules surrounded below by a persistent sepal-cup. The fruits are oblong, about 3 cm long and 1.5 cm wide. The capsules are yellow-green in colour and glaucous at first, then at maturity they turn dark brown. The fruit calyx is woody and 5 toothed.
fruit.text_html:

flower.text: The flowers of Lagerstroemia parviflora are bisexual, small and white in colour. They grow in axillary or terminal panicles of 2 to 6 flowers clusters. Each flower is less than 5 mm wide with a 1 cm long pedicel. The calyx-tube is 7 mm long with a ring inside. Each flower has 6 circular flat petals, white in colour. Many stamens inserted near the base of the calyx tube are longer than the rest. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:

leaf.text: The leaves of Lagerstroemia parviflora are simple, decussate with an opposite arrangement. They are broadly obovate-elliptic in shape. The leaves are 3 to 8 cm long and 2 cm wide. The leaves are thin coriaceous. The leaf base is cuneate-subacute and the leaf apex is obtuse-retuse. The leaf margin is entire. The petiole is less than 1 cm long. The leaves are glaucous in the lower side.

habit.text: Lagerstroemia parviflora is a medium sized deciduous tree growing up to 10 m in height. It is a beautiful drought resistant tree.
habit.text_html:
Lagerstroemia parviflora is a medium sized deciduous tree growing up to 10 m in height. 
It is a beautiful drought resistant tree.
